title: Hiring and training Pearl Bailey
summary: He hired Pearl after hearing her at a rehearsal for her different voice, and pushed her to do it his way.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh, he was going with Pearl Bailey then.
Oh.
I think. Yeah.
Yeah.
Yeah.
And was Pearl with the -- in your band?
I don't know. I don't think so. But
that was his girl friend.
Well, around what time did you -- did Pearl come and sing with the band? Did she come around because he was in the band, and you started to -- and you heard her, or what?
Where did I hear Pearl? I heard Pearl in a rehearsal, too.
Did you?
Yeah. And I said, 'That's what I want.' And that's when I hired Pearl Bailey.
Well, you know, funnily enough, thinking that, you know, we were talking about singers before, but Pearl is another one of that type of singer that she's better in person than on a record. Right?
-- than on a record.
She comes across. What she offers is, well, it's a personality thing, to a great extent, isn't it?
Yeah.
But she's got a good ear, though, hasn't she?
Yeah. And she had something different. Her voice was different, and that's what attracted my attention to her.
What -- a low voice?
Yeah.
A throaty voice.
Yeah. She was different.
Yeah.
Quite different from all the other singers around. The female singers.
Yeah.
And that attracted my attention, right there.
Yeah.
And that's the reason why I wanted her.
Yeah. She hadn't sung with a band then, had she?
No. Not when I first heard her. You know, when she came into rehearse over something. She sang something and that's when I hired her.
Now, her brother was the dancer, wasn't he?
Yeah. Her brother was a dancer.
He was a good dancer, too.
Oh, yeah.
Well, Pearl danced too, didn't she?
Yeah.
Yeah.
Yeah. Pearl was a good dancer.
Well, so you hired her. Well, what was it
I had a very hard time with Pearl.
How come?
Bringing out within her what she had. It wasn't an easy job.
Why?
It just wasn't an easy job. She'd say, 'Well, I can't do this this way.' And I'd say, 'Well, you're going to do it this way.' And I made her do it that way.
Why, what kind of way would she want to do it? She'd want to be conventional or something?
But she didn't have no way, because she was going to do it my way. And I made her do it my way. And that's the reason why she became a success.
Well --
I was rehearsing that band about every day, and her.
Really?
Yeah. That's right.
Can you think of any particular numbers, to give me an idea?

No. Everything that she did. If she wasn't doing it right, like I wanted it did, I would tell her. And I said, 'No, it don't go like that. Do it this way. Do it this way. Do it this way.' I would sweat her out.
(Laughter)
She didn't take to it kindly, huh?
No, no.
(Laughter)
That's funny. But nevertheless, she must have know you were right, Cootie.
Well, in the end. She thanks me today.
She does thank you today.
Uh-huh.
No kidding. How long did she stay with the band?
She stayed with the band quite a while, until Count Basie got a job at a theater around there on Broadway. And somebody told --
